sections.content:
## What You'll Learn

By the end of this lesson `claude --version` will return a version number, `claude` will launch Claude Code in your terminal, and you'll understand your billing options. You'll also configure your first session settings.

## Prerequisites

**Node.js (v18 or later):** Claude Code is a Node.js package, so Node.js must be installed. Check if you already have it:

```powershell
node --version
```

If this returns `v18.x.x` or higher — skip the Node.js install. If you see an error or a version below 18:

1. Go to **nodejs.org**
2. Click the **LTS** download button (stable version)
3. Run the installer, keeping all defaults
4. When finished, close and reopen PowerShell
5. Run `node --version` again — should show v20.x.x or higher

**npm** (comes with Node.js — no separate install needed):
```powershell
npm --version
```
Should show a version number.

## Installing Claude Code

With Node.js in place, Claude Code installs in one command:

```powershell
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```

The `-g` flag installs it globally — the `claude` command becomes available from any directory.

**If you get a permissions error:** Open PowerShell as Administrator (search PowerShell → right-click → Run as Administrator), then re-run the command.

Installation takes 1-3 minutes. You'll see output ending with something like `added 847 packages`.

**Verify the install:**
```powershell
claude --version
```
You should see a version number like `1.x.x`. If you see `command not recognized`, close PowerShell and reopen it — the PATH sometimes needs a fresh shell to update.

**Update Claude Code when new versions release:**
```powershell
npm update -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```
Anthropic releases updates frequently — run this every few weeks to stay current.

## Authentication and Billing Options

The first time you launch Claude Code, it needs to authenticate. There are two ways:

**Option 1 — Claude.ai subscription (Max plan):**
If you subscribe to Claude Max ($100/month), Claude Code is included with high usage limits. This is the recommended option if you plan to use Claude Code heavily — predictable cost, no token counting.

Authenticate:
1. Run `claude` in the terminal
2. Select the option to authenticate via Claude.ai
3. A browser window opens — sign in to your Claude.ai account
4. The browser redirects back to the terminal — you're authenticated

**Option 2 — Anthropic API (pay per use):**
Get an API key from console.anthropic.com (free account, add a payment method). This is pay-as-you-go — charged per token you use.

Authenticate:
1. Go to console.anthropic.com
2. Create an account (or sign in)
3. Go to API Keys → Create Key
4. Copy the key (starts with `sk-ant-`)
5. In the terminal: `export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY='your-key-here'` (PowerShell: `$env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY='your-key-here'`)
6. Or run `claude` and it will prompt you to enter the key interactively

**Cost for learning use:** Typical learning use (Part 7 exercises) runs $3-15 total on the API. Most individual coding sessions cost $0.10-0.50.

**Option 3 — VS Code Extension (alternative to CLI):**
Install the Claude Code extension from the VS Code marketplace. It uses the same authentication as the CLI and provides a UI panel inside VS Code. For learning, still recommend the CLI first — you see exactly what's happening.

## First Launch and Interface Overview

Once authenticated, launch Claude Code:

```powershell
claude
```

You'll see a welcome message and a prompt:
```
╭─────────────────────────────────╮
│  Claude Code (v1.x.x)           │
│  Type a message or /help        │
╰─────────────────────────────────╯

>
```

**The REPL (Read-Eval-Print Loop):** You're now in an interactive session where you type requests and Claude Code responds. Unlike chat, Claude Code has access to your filesystem from the current directory.

**Key commands:**

```
/help          — show all available commands
/status        — show current session info (tokens used, files read)
/compact       — compress conversation history to save context
/clear         — clear conversation and start fresh
/exit          — exit Claude Code
/model         — see or switch the model being used
```

**Slash commands for tasks:**
```
/read [file]   — tell Claude Code to read a specific file
/memory        — show what Claude Code remembers about this project
```

**The permission system:** By default, Claude Code asks for permission before:
- Writing or modifying files
- Running terminal commands
- Making network requests

You'll see prompts like: `[Y]es / [N]o / [A]lways allow`. Respond thoughtfully — don't set 'Always allow' for destructive operations without understanding what they do.

## Running Claude Code Properly: Open in Your Project

Claude Code reads files relative to the directory it's launched from. Always launch it from inside your project:

```powershell
cd C:\Projects\Learning\my-project
claude
```

Or in File Explorer: Shift+right-click your project folder → Open in Terminal → then run `claude`.

**Why this matters:** If you launch Claude Code from `C:\`, it'll have the wrong context for your files. If you launch from inside your project directory, it automatically knows the folder structure and can find all your files.

**The `--print` flag for quick one-off tasks:**
```powershell
claude --print "What does the main function in main.js do?"
```
This runs a single question and exits without entering the interactive REPL. Useful for quick checks.

**Never paste API keys into Claude Code conversations.** Your ANTHROPIC_API_KEY should live in an environment variable or in Claude Code's credential store — not in your project files or chat messages. The security habit from lesson 1-5 applies here: credentials in conversation text are credentials at risk.

sections.title: Full Install and First Session
sections.content:
Work through every step. Don't move on until each produces the expected output.

**Step 1 — Verify Node.js:**
```powershell
node --version
```
Expected: `v18.x.x` or higher. If error, install from nodejs.org first.

**Step 2 — Install Claude Code:**
```powershell
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```
Wait for completion. Expected: `added X packages` at the end.

**Step 3 — Verify:**
```powershell
claude --version
```
Expected: a version number.

**Step 4 — Navigate to your course project folder:**
```powershell
cd C:\Projects\Learning
```
(Or wherever you created your course folder in lesson 4-2)

**Step 5 — Launch Claude Code:**
```powershell
claude
```
Follow the authentication prompts. Choose the option that matches how you want to pay (Claude.ai subscription or API key).

**Step 6 — Explore the interface:**
Once authenticated, type these inside the Claude Code REPL:
```
/help
```
Read through the commands carefully — you'll use most of these in Part 7.

```
/status
```
See your current session information.

Then ask your first real question:
```
What files are in the current directory? Describe what this project is.
```
Claude Code will list the files it can see and describe what the project appears to be.

**Step 7 — Exit:**
```
/exit
```

**You're done if:** `claude --version` returns a version number and `claude` launches without an authentication error.

**Troubleshooting:**
- `command not found`: close and reopen PowerShell (PATH update needed)
- Permission error during install: run PowerShell as Administrator
- Authentication fails: try `/logout` then `claude` again, or re-enter your API key

sections.question: You've just installed Claude Code and are setting it up for the first time. You have a Claude.ai free tier account but haven't set up API billing. What are your options for authenticating?
options: You can't use Claude Code without a paid plan — the CLI requires enterprise access
You can authenticate with your Claude.ai account (subscribing to Max covers the CLI) or get an API key from console.anthropic.com (pay-as-you-go)
You authenticate only with an API key — Claude.ai accounts don't work with the CLI
The free tier automatically provides Claude Code access with 50 messages per day
sections.explanation: There are two authentication paths: (1) Claude Max subscription connects your Claude.ai account and includes Claude Code usage in the monthly plan — best for heavy use. (2) An Anthropic API key from console.anthropic.com allows pay-as-you-go billing — best for occasional use or learning. The free tier doesn't include Claude Code API access, but new API accounts often get free credits to start.

sections.title: Workshop A — Install and Verify Claude Code
sections.content:
This drill gets Claude Code installed and running your first command.

**Step 1 — Install Claude Code:**
```powershell
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```
(Requires Node.js 18+. Run `node --version` first.)

**Step 2 — Verify installation:**
```powershell
claude --version
```

**Step 3 — Authenticate:**
```powershell
claude
```
Follow the authentication flow (browser-based OAuth to your Claude account).

**Step 4 — Run your first command in a project folder:**
```powershell
cd your-project-folder
claude
```
In the Claude Code interface, type: "What files are in this project?"

**Step 5 — Verify it can read your project:** Ask: "Summarise what this project does based on the files you can see."

**Step 6 — Exit Claude Code:** Type /exit or press Ctrl+C.

sections.title: Workshop B — First Real Claude Code Task
sections.content:
Complete your first real Claude Code task — something genuinely useful.

**Step 1 — Open Claude Code in a real project:**
```powershell
cd your-real-project
claude
```

**Step 2 — Give Claude Code a real, specific task** from your project (use your ranked list from Lesson 7-1 Workshop D). Keep it to something that should take under 10 minutes:
- "Add a README.md to this project based on what you see in the files"
- "Add docstrings to all functions in [filename]"
- "Find any TODO comments in the codebase and list them"

**Step 3 — Watch Claude Code work.** Notice: which tools does it use? Which files does it read? What commands does it run?

**Step 4 — Review the output.** Is what Claude Code produced correct and useful?

**Step 5 — Mandatory review:** In the Claude Code session, type: *"Review what you just did. What might be wrong or incomplete? What didn't you do that I might have expected?"*

**Step 6 — Commit the result** with a descriptive message.

sections.title: Workshop C — Claude Code Permission Modes
sections.content:
Claude Code's permission system controls what it can do autonomously. Understanding it prevents surprises.

**Step 1 — Read the permission documentation:**
```powershell
claude --help
```
Or ask Claude.ai: "What are Claude Code's permission modes? What does each mode allow and prevent?"

**Step 2 — Start Claude Code in conservative mode** (does not execute commands without approval):
```powershell
claude --permission-mode=default
```

**Step 3 — Give it a task that requires running code.** Notice that it asks for permission before executing.

**Step 4 — Compare:** Start a new session without permission restrictions. Give the same task. How does the behaviour differ?

**Step 5 — Ask Claude:** *"For a developer working on a production codebase, what permission mode should they use for Claude Code? What are the risks of using fully autonomous mode?"*

**Step 6 — Set your default:** Based on what you learned, what permission mode will you use by default?

sections.title: Workshop D — Configure Claude Code for Your Environment
sections.content:
Configure Claude Code to work best in your specific development environment.

**Step 1 — Check your Claude Code version and settings:**
```powershell
claude --version
claude config
```

**Step 2 — Configure your model preference:**
```powershell
claude config set model claude-sonnet-4-6
```

**Step 3 — Set up a CLAUDE.md** in your main project (we'll cover this in depth in Lesson 7-6, but start now):
- Create `CLAUDE.md` in your project root
- Add 3 basic things: what the project is, the main language/framework, and one thing Claude Code should always do (e.g., "Always run tests after making changes")

**Step 4 — Test the configuration:** Start a Claude Code session and ask it to do a task. Does it follow your CLAUDE.md instruction?

**Step 5 — Mandatory setup review:** Ask Claude: *"Review my Claude Code setup. What configuration or CLAUDE.md instructions should I add to make Claude Code more reliable for [your project type]?"*

sections.question: You install Claude Code but the `claude` command is not found in your terminal. What is the most likely cause?
options: Claude Code requires a paid API subscription
npm did not add the global package location to your system PATH — you need to fix your PATH or use npx claude
Claude Code is only for Mac/Linux
You need to restart your computer
sections.explanation: When npm installs a global package (`npm install -g`), it places the executable in a global npm bin directory. If this directory isn't in your system PATH, the command won't be found. The fix on Windows: run `npm config get prefix` to find where npm installs globals, then add that path + \node_modules\.bin to your system PATH. Alternatively, use `npx @anthropic-ai/claude-code` to run without global installation.

sections.question: Why is it important to create a CLAUDE.md file in your project before running Claude Code on it?
options: Claude Code won't work without a CLAUDE.md file
CLAUDE.md provides persistent project context — without it, Claude Code has to re-discover your project structure and conventions every session, leading to less consistent results
CLAUDE.md sets the permission mode for the session
sections.explanation: CLAUDE.md is a persistent instruction file that Claude Code reads at the start of every session. It gives Claude Code: project purpose and architecture, conventions and style rules, what to avoid, commands to run for testing/building. Without it, you spend time re-establishing context each session and risk Claude Code making decisions that don't fit your project's conventions. It's project memory for the agent.

sections.content: **You've completed lesson 7-2.** Claude Code is installed and authenticated. You understand the billing options and the interface basics. In the next lesson you'll use it on a real project for the first time.
